reason: First quote states the Docker CLI lacks native IAM authentication so extra steps are needed; second quote says to run aws ecr get-login-password to authenticate Docker to an ECR registry.
Quote states the ECS or Fargate container agent must have permissions for ecr:BatchGetImage, ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer and ecr:GetAuthorizationToken for tasks to pull from ECR private repositories.
Quotes state images are stored in ECR-managed S3 buckets, default SSE-S3 with AES-256, no action needed, no additional charge, and SSE-KMS for more control.
Under the FAQ heading 'Can I share my images across AWS accounts?' the quote answers yes and points to an example policy for cross-account image sharing.
Quote states anyone with or without an AWS account can use the ECR public gallery to search for and download common images and files such as Helm charts.
Quote states IAM resource-based policies control and monitor who and what can access images, and how, when and where, created for your repositories.

The quota row gives 4,200 as the value in each supported Region but does not say per what (described only as 'maximum number of layer parts'); the claim reads it as a Regional total of layer parts, a per-what the quote does not carry.
Three quotes state lifecycle policies give more control in a private repository, images expire within 24 hours after meeting criteria, and the preview should be used before applying.
Quotes state the one-time copy applies where pull through cache is not supported, ECR stores the copied version and newer versions are not pulled automatically.
Quote states ECR checks whether the cached image was validated upstream within the last 24 hours and, if expired, checks upstream and updates the cache.
The lead-in quote and the three list-line quotes give exactly the three groups of upstream registries and their authentication requirements as claimed.
Quota row: 25 rules per replication configuration, not adjustable; What's New quotes give the rise from 10 to 25 per registry and the Aug 17, 2026 post date.
Quote states by default only the creating account has access and a repository policy can allow additional access.
Quotes cover the subset statement, deny-in-either-means-denied, allow via either suffices, and the IAM-policy requirement for ecr:GetAuthorizationToken.
First quote supports preventing overwrites via tag immutability; second quote, under the console heading, supports the Immutable tag exclusion box for a few immutable tags.
Quote in the ECS Anywhere FAQ states one configurable key can register from 1 up to 1,000 VMs or bare metal servers.
Quotes state tasks keep running on connectivity loss, keep reaching AWS services while task role credentials are active (default 6 hours), and cannot after expiry until reconnection.
Quotes state opting in to awsvpcTrunking gives supported EC2 Linux instances a higher ENI quota and more tasks per instance, with container agent 1.28.1 or later.
Quote states ECS continuously monitors AZ task distribution and rebalances by launching tasks in the AZs with fewest tasks and terminating in overloaded AZs.
Quote states a cluster can mix all capacity provider types but a capacity provider strategy can't mix different types.

The feature is scoped to container instances with impaired agent connectivity (AGENT_CONNECTIVITY event, per the post title); the claim drops that trigger and reads as general detect-and-repair of container instances.
Quotes give the Feb 19, 2025 post date and the increase to up to 192 vCPU for ECS tasks on EC2 from the previous 10 vCPU limit.
Quote states value times desired count, clamped to minimum 3 and maximum 200, and that this is the default type with default value 50.

Both quotes describe the scale-out and scale-in paths via CapacityProviderReservation, the CloudWatch alarm, DesiredCapacity, launch/register and terminate/deregister, with the at-least-one-instance condition.
Quote matches the claim word for word.
Quotes from the Fargate task definition parameters and Fargate clusters pages give the definition, the platform version 1.3.0 requirement, default 30 seconds and maximum 120 seconds.
Quotes state the three distinct layers and that the orchestration layer schedules and scales your environment.
Quotes state organizations might choose managed container services to reduce overhead and that many customers want portability, including on premises and in the cloud.
Quotes state attached EBS volumes are managed by ECS, can be new or loaded from snapshots, and can be encrypted with AWS KMS keys.
Quote states no additional charge for Express Mode and you pay only for underlying resources.
Quotes state the sensible-defaults purpose and the three required inputs, each list line quoted under the Express Mode heading.
Quotes state public or private HTTPS support with auto scaling, and the web applications and APIs scenario.
Quote matches the claim: CUR cost data for ECS tasks on EC2 by opting into Split Cost Allocation Data.
Under the FAQ heading on configuring container instances to pull from ECR, the quote gives the task definition repository plus AmazonEC2ContainerServiceforEC2Role.
Quotes under the Express Mode FAQ state full access to underlying resources and modifying them via Console, API or CLI.
Quote states vCPU and memory requested, from image pull to task termination, rounded up to the second, one-minute minimum.
Quote states VPC mode assigns each running task a dedicated elastic networking interface with full VPC networking features like EC2.
Quote names both metrics and states Application Auto Scaling uses them with scaling policies to scale task count proportionally.
Quota row lists 125 for named Regions, 500 for other Regions, not adjustable, per service per minute, and 125 for Regions introduced after May 20, 2025.
Quote matches every clause: PrivateLink, private IPs, traffic kept on the Amazon network, no IGW, NAT or VGW needed.
Under the heading for Regions introduced starting December 23, 2023, the quotes require the listed Region-specific endpoints and say traffic goes public if not all are configured.
Quote states host images in the same Region, ECR is available in every ECS Region, and avoid traversing the internet or VPN.
Quotes state launch type to launch type updates are not supported and EC2 to Fargate uses the Fargate capacity provider instead.
Quotes state draining after 14 days for up-to-date patches and the secure configuration with no SSH, immutable root filesystem and SELinux.
Quotes state multiple tasks per instance by default unlike Fargate, and optional one-task-per-instance VM-level isolation.
Quotes state two IAM roles are required and define the infrastructure role and the instance profile as claimed.
Quotes cover terminating only instances without running tasks, the DAEMON exception, and the scale-in protection prerequisite.
Quotes give the no-load-balancer scope and the 40-second wait after RUNNING when no essential container has a health check.
Quote defines random, spread and binpack exactly as claimed.
Quotes state past load data for daily or weekly patterns, proactive task increase, and the three situations where it is most useful.

The 52% sits under the heading 'Compute Savings Plans for Fargate' and the adjacent table ties up to ~52% to the 3-year term (1-year up to ~17-26%); the claim drops both and reads as up to 52% for a 1-year or 3-year term.

The claim names Managed Instances as the exception, but the same pricing page's Details table also lists ECS Anywhere with a flat per-instance fee ($0.01025 per registered on-premises instance/hour), so the exception list is incomplete.
Quote states credentials stored in Secrets Manager and referenced in the task definition for private registries outside AWS, supported on Fargate, EC2 and ECS Anywhere.
Quotes state scale out before the demand shock because autoscaling takes time, and over-provision for unscheduled shocks.

The page says secrets can be referenced as any of three options (secrets env variables, secretOptions, repositoryCredentials); the claim presents environment variables via secrets as the way they are referenced, dropping that it is one option.
Quotes state ELB is recommended for internet connections and Service Connect for service-to-service without a load balancer, with short names and standard ports.
Quotes state Service Connect suits connections within the same namespace and each service can belong to only one namespace.
Quotes list Service Connect, service discovery via Route 53 namespace and DNS, and VPC Lattice with a cost, as ways without a load balancer.
Quote matches: ECS syncs launched tasks to Cloud Map, which maintains a DNS hostname resolving to task internal IPs.
Quote matches: the main disadvantage is extra retry and failure logic, and DNS records have a TTL controlling caching.
Quotes state a service can move from launch type to capacity provider strategy with a forced new deployment, and ASG to Fargate capacity provider updates (and the reverse) are not possible.
Both quotes come from the page for ECS Linux container instances; the claim generalizes the DRAINING behavior and off-by-default to all ECS Spot container instances, a scope the quotes do not carry.
Quote matches every clause: scale-in can stop a processing task, risk of reprocessing or lost progress, and task scale-in protection as the fix.
Quote states you can update a service's capacity provider strategy to move it from one compute type to the other.
Quotes state targetCapacity below 100% represents free EC2 capacity and spare capacity speeds future task launches.
Quotes give the depends-on-requirements statement and the listed use cases with their hosting scopes (Fargate/Managed Instances/external for ECR and awslogs; Fargate/EC2 for secrets).
Quotes state no EC2 instance profiles on Fargate, task roles irrespective of compute option with SDK or CLI, and CloudTrail shows which task got the credentials.
Quota row: 5,000 tasks per service (desired count), not adjustable; note quote: 1,000 per service with service discovery due to the Cloud Map quota.
Quotes state access entries are recommended at or after the listed platform version, migration of ConfigMap entries is recommended, and earlier versions must use aws-auth.
Quote matches: curated set of add-ons, latest security patches and bug fixes, validated by AWS.
Quote matches the claim word for word.
Quotes state the 21-day reducible maximum lifetime with replacement, SELinux enforcing and read-only root file system, and no SSH or SSM access.
Quotes state self-managed clusters with 60-70 percent maintenance time and the outcomes including an 80 percent compute cost cut.
Quotes give the Mar 5, 2025 date, previously optional KMS provider v1, now default for all API objects, AWS-owned keys by default, and automatic for 1.28 or higher.
Quotes give the Mar 20, 2026 date and the 99.99% SLA for Provisioned Control Plane up from 99.95% on standard control plane.
Quote matches the claim word for word.
Quotes state EKS fully manages Auto Mode node rollback with a configurable timeout, default 12 hours, maximum 7 days.
Quotes state the role is required for Pods on Fargate, why (AWS API calls such as ECR pulls and log routing), and that a Fargate profile must specify it.
Quotes state at least one Fargate profile is required and Pods matching a selector by namespace and labels are scheduled on Fargate.
Quote matches: reliable connection required, not a fit for DDIL environments, consider EKS Anywhere.
